correctness.rationale: For every deterministic periodic binary-delay word with a fresh step, matrices T0=v e1^T and T1 define the recurrence exactly. Every period monodromy has eigenvalues 0 and product of p_L for its cyclic runs. Floquet stability is strict modulus below one; Cayley–Hamilton yields at most two-period annihilation when product zero. The run recurrence matches the determinant of a path adjacency pencil, giving positive simple cosine roots and the parity-dependent quadratic growth of the largest root. For the period-three word, the two exact inequalities give precisely (0,1) union (2,3). The supplied checker verifies 502 period words, nine path determinants/root formulas and exact golden-ratio nilpotence; none replaces the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Controlled binary staleness is a natural benchmark for asynchronous quadratic descent. The exact all-period classification is an algorithmic design invariant computable from run lengths; the shortest nontrivial word already has a disconnected admissible stepsize set, and lengthened stale runs exhibit unbounded but precisely tuned finite-time cancellation. These distinguish temporally scheduled delays from a monotone conservative stepsize bound. The statement does not infer practical robustness; its boundary phenomenon and complete natural classification are substantive beyond an isolated numerical example.
